title: The Grand Loop: Cliff Monasteries, the Prut and the Deep South by Car
subRegion: Dniester cliffs, the northern Prut, Ștefan Vodă and Gagauzia

bestPeriod.window: the second half of September — harvest in the vineyards, dry clay tracks, and the Prut floodplain still green
bestPeriod.avoid: March–April and any wet spell (village clay roads become impassable), and mid-July to mid-August (35 °C, dust)

gatewayAirport: Chișinău International (KIV). Collect the car at the airport; Moldovan-plated rentals need no road vignette. Iași (IAS) in Romania is a viable alternative entry, 2 h 30 from Chișinău, but a cross-border hire costs more.
summary: Roughly 1,050 km around a country the size of Belgium, on roads that change character every twenty minutes: fresh EU-funded asphalt, then broken Soviet concrete slab, then a clay farm track with a horse cart on it.…
hook: Roughly 1,050 km around a country the size of Belgium, on roads that change character every twenty minutes: fresh EU-funded asphalt, then broken Soviet concrete slab, then a clay farm track with a horse cart on it. In between are rock-hewn monasteries cut into Dniester limestone, a circular Genoese-plan fortress at Soroca, a hundred hills on the Prut floodplain that geologists still argue about, and the best wine you have never been offered.

snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV). Collect the car at the airport; Moldovan-plated rentals need no road vignette. Iași (IAS) in Romania is a viable alternative entry, 2 h 30 from Chișinău, but a cross-border hire costs more.

itinerary.title: Out of the city to the Răut meander
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at KIV and take the M2 north, then the R20 down into the Răut valley. Traffic thins within twenty minutes of the ring road.
itinerary.afternoon: **Orheiul Vechi**: the cave monastery cut into the limestone spur above Butuceni, a working hermitage reached through a rock passage, with the Răut wrapping the promontory below. Entry **20 MDL** adult, 10 MDL reduced; the Butuceni information point runs 08:00–18:00 weekdays and to 20:00 at weekends. A guide for 1–10 people is 200 MDL in Romanian, 300 MDL in English.
itinerary.evening: Stay in **Butuceni** or **Trebujeni**. Dinner is *plăcinte*, *zeamă* and house wine from a plastic jug, and the sky over the meander is very dark.

itinerary.title: Two cliff monasteries
itinerary.morning: North to **Saharna** via Rezina. The monastery complex sits at the mouth of a gorge; the marked path upstream past the cascades to the **Grimidon** rock and the old rock-hewn skete is about 3 km each way, easy but slippery on wet limestone.
itinerary.afternoon: South-east to **Țipova** — the **largest rock-hewn monastery in Eastern Europe**, three levels of cells and a church carved into the cliff perhaps 250 m above the Dniester, with a steep stair down to the water and a waterfall gorge behind the village.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at the Saharna monastery guesthouse or a Lalova pension. Neither has a card machine [VERIFY: current Saharna and Țipova monastery guesthouse rates].

itinerary.title: To the fortress
itinerary.morning: North on the R20 and M2 through Rezina, Șoldănești and Florești. This stretch shows the road spectrum in one morning: new asphalt, then a slab section, then new asphalt again.
itinerary.afternoon: **Soroca fortress**, the best-preserved castle in Moldova — a **perfect circle** with five towers, rebuilt in stone in the 1540s under Petru Rareș on a Genoese-influenced plan, standing directly on the Dniester bank with Ukraine 300 m across the water.
itinerary.evening: Walk up to the hill of **Roma mansions** above the town — a genuinely strange skyline of self-built palaces with Bolshoi and Capitol domes — then eat by the river [VERIFY: current Soroca fortress entry fee and hours].

itinerary.title: The Prut floodplain
itinerary.morning: West through **Bălți**, Moldova's second city — a place to refuel and buy provisions rather than to sightsee — then south-west to Glodeni.
itinerary.afternoon: **Pădurea Domnească**, the "Princely Forest": the country's largest floodplain oak forest on the Prut, arranged through **Moldsilva** in advance (+373 22 27 23 06). Five **European bison** live in a fenced enclosure reachable only with a warden, and the established route "Pe un picior de plai pe-o gură de rai" runs through the old oaks. No published tariff — it is settled in cash on arrival [VERIFY: current Pădurea Domnească visit fee].
itinerary.evening: The **Suta de Movile** — the "Hundred Hills" — near Cobani: a field of several hundred low mounds spread across the Prut terrace, origin still disputed between reef remnants and landslip. Best at low sun from the R16 above the village.

itinerary.title: South again, and underground
itinerary.morning: The long run back down the R16 and M14 through Ungheni to Chișinău. Fuel in Ungheni; the north has real gaps in the network.
itinerary.afternoon: **Castel Mimi** at Bulboaca, a restored 1893 château of the last governor of Bessarabia, now a working winery with gardens and a restaurant [VERIFY: current Castel Mimi tour and tasting prices]; or **Cricova**, 15 km from the capital, 120 km of galleries toured **by vehicle** — Matinal 250 MDL, tasting tours 400–3,100 MDL, reservation mandatory.
itinerary.evening: A night in Chișinău, laundry, and an ATM stop before the south.

itinerary.title: Ștefan Vodă and the deep south
itinerary.morning: East and south to **Purcari** in the **Ștefan Vodă** appellation, Moldova's most decorated estate, founded 1827. Advance booking is required: château tour 300 MDL, Classic tasting 450 MDL, Reserve Exclusive 600 MDL, with minimum party sizes on the higher tastings. Note the road east of Căușeni runs close to the de facto line — stay on the signed M3 and do not improvise a shortcut.
itinerary.afternoon: West across the southern steppe to **Slobozia Mare** on the Prut. This is the emptiest driving of the week: long straight roads, sunflower to the horizon, villages of geese.
itinerary.evening: **Prutul de Jos** reserve HQ (tel 062122295): two set routes — a **3 km, 2-hour walking route** to the Beleu viewing platform, and a **boat route through the Manolescu channel** onto **Lake Beleu**, run only when water levels allow and in small groups. Binoculars are lent; there is camping and a dining pavilion at HQ. Arrange by phone at least a day ahead.

itinerary.title: Beleu, Gagauzia, home
itinerary.morning: Dawn on **Lake Beleu**, the largest natural lake in Moldova and the core of a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve on the lower Prut — pelicans, glossy ibis, herons, and in autumn migrating waterfowl in numbers.
itinerary.afternoon: North-east to **Comrat**, capital of **Găgăuzia**. The Gagauz National History and Ethnography Museum and a plate of *gözleme* and *kıvırma* are a good last stop before the motorway-grade run home.
itinerary.evening: M3 north to Chișinău, 100 km and 1 h 45. Refuel before returning the car — Moldovan rentals are full-to-full and airport fuel is dearer.

accommodationStrategy.name: Butuceni village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: five minutes from the Orheiul Vechi cave monastery on the reserve side of the river, with secure yard parking, home-cooked half board, and the Belvedere platform for sunrise before any day-tripper arrives from the capital.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–4 weeks ahead; the village has only a few dozen beds and the capital's weekend traffic takes them.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel in Soroca centre
accommodationStrategy.description: the only proper hotel base in the north, five minutes' walk from the fortress and the river promenade, with off-street parking — which matters, because street parking near the fortress is informal and unlit.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 1–2 weeks ahead; midweek is always available.

accommodationStrategy.name: Prutul de Jos reserve accommodation / Slobozia Mare pensions
accommodationStrategy.description: puts you at the lake for the dawn boat window rather than driving two hours to reach it, with camping and a dining pavilion at the reserve HQ and a warden who can tell you at 06:00 whether the channel is navigable.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by phone with the reserve (062122295 / 062122289) at least a few days ahead; there is no online system.

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is **not** in EU roaming — buy an Orange or Moldcell SIM at KIV. Coverage is good on the M-roads and adequate in villages; download offline maps, because satnav routing on the R-roads will confidently send you down a clay track.
logistics.emergency: **112** nationwide, with English usually available. Give your position by village name and R-road number. Recovery from a soft clay track is a tractor and a negotiation, not a service call — budget 500–1,000 MDL and expect it to take two hours.
logistics.weather: The whole plan pivots on rain. A single heavy shower closes the clay legs for 24–48 hours; check the forecast the night before each dirt section and use the alternatives above without regret. Summer heat over 35 °C is normal in the south, where there is no shade at all.
logistics.bookingWindows: Purcari, Cricova and Castel Mimi are reservation-only, several days out. The Moldsilva and Prutul de Jos reserve visits need a phone call days ahead. Village guesthouses 2–4 weeks in season.
logistics.money: Moldovan leu, roughly 19–20 MDL to the euro. Cards work in Chișinău, Bălți, Soroca and Comrat and at the named wineries; village guesthouses, monastery donations, reserve fees and roadside melon stalls are **cash**. Carry 3,000–5,000 MDL. ATMs exist in every raion centre, not in villages.
logistics.transportRules: **Zero-tolerance drink-driving — the legal limit is effectively 0.00 and enforcement is routine.** Dipped headlights outside built-up areas. Seatbelts front and rear. Speed 50 in villages, 90 rural, 110 on the few dual sections. **Livestock and horse carts roam free** and are at their worst at dusk when herds return to the village — an unlit cart on an unlit road is the single most likely accident on this trip. Do not drive rural roads after dark if you can avoid it.
logistics.permits: No permits for ordinary roads. **The scientific reserves — Codrii, Pădurea Domnească, Prutul de Jos — are not walk-up sites**; access is by prior arrangement with each administration and fees are settled in cash. Orheiul Vechi charges 20 MDL. Foreign-plated cars need the **vinieta**; Moldovan-plated rentals do not.

proTips: **Treat rain as a routing decision, not an inconvenience.** Check the forecast each evening and reorder the next day around it — Țipova, Suta de Movile and the Beleu dyke are all wet-weather no-gos, and all three have a dry-foot alternative.
**Fuel above half a tank north of Bălți.** Stations thin out towards Glodeni and Cobani, several close at 20:00, and a few village pumps take cash only.
**Leave the rental in Chișinău for Transnistria.** Your insurance almost certainly excludes it; a rutieră from Gara Centrală costs about 50 MDL and removes the entire problem.
**Ask the guesthouse to phone ahead for you.** Reserve wardens, monastery guesthouses and small wineries answer a Romanian call from a local number far more reliably than an email in English.

**Buy directly from the small producers you drive past.** Moldova's best-value bottles are sold at the gate for a third of the Chișinău restaurant price, and *vin de casă* in a refilled plastic bottle is a genuine local institution — just remember rule 6 below.
**Nobody drinks and drives here, at all.** With a zero limit and frequent checks, the practical answer is one driver who tastes nothing, or a night in the village where the winery is.
**Do Beleu at dawn and Suta de Movile at dusk.** Both are low-relief landscapes that only read in raking light; in flat midday sun they photograph as nothing at all.

raw.Driving legs, km and time: Chișinău → **Orheiul Vechi (Trebujeni/Butuceni)** 60 km / 1 h 15. Orheiul Vechi → **Saharna** 60 km / 1 h 20 via Rezina. Saharna → **Țipova** 35 km / 1 h (the last 6 km is track). Țipova → **Soroca** 110 km / 2 h 15. Soroca → **Bălți** 45 km / 1 h. Bălți → **Pădurea Domnească** (Cuhnești/Branişte) 55 km / 1 h 15. Pădurea Domnească → **Suta de Movile** (Cobani/Braniște) 15 km / 30 min. Cobani → Chișinău 175 km / 3 h. Chișinău → **Castel Mimi** (Bulboaca) 40 km / 45 min. Castel Mimi → **Purcari** 80 km / 1 h 30. Purcari → **Slobozia Mare (Lake Beleu)** 165 km / 3 h. Slobozia Mare → **Comrat** 110 km / 2 h. Comrat → Chișinău 100 km / 1 h 45.
raw.Road reality — the core of this trip: Moldova has three road surfaces and you will meet all of them daily. **M-roads** (M2 Chișinău–Soroca, M3 south, M14) are mostly resurfaced two-lane asphalt at 90 km/h and are fine. **R-roads** run the full range: recently rebuilt EU- and EBRD-funded asphalt on some sections, and **unrepaired Soviet concrete slab** on others — the slab is the worst surface here, with 3–5 cm joints every few metres that will shake the car apart above 50 km/h. **Village *drum de țară*** are unsealed clay: perfectly drivable when dry in a normal hatchback, and **genuinely impassable within an hour of rain**, when the clay turns to grease and even 4x4s slide off camber. Plan every dirt leg with an alternative.
raw.Wet-weather alternatives for each dirt l: *Țipova approach:* the direct descent from Horodiște is clay — in wet weather park in Horodiște village and walk the 2 km down, or approach from Lalova on the river road. *Saharna gorge track:* leave the car at the monastery car park on asphalt and walk the waterfall gorge; do not drive the upper track. *Suta de Movile:* the field tracks between the mounds are pure clay — in the wet, view them from the R16 above Cobani and skip the interior. *Pădurea Domnească:* the forest roads are the warden's problem, not yours; the reserve visit is by warden vehicle or on foot. *Beleu:* the Manolescu channel access is a dyke road that softens badly; ask the reserve HQ before driving it.
raw.Rental cross-border rules: **Romania is normally permitted** with advance notice, a **Green Card** and a cross-border fee. **Ukraine is normally excluded** from Moldovan rental insurance, and so is **Transnistria** — critical, because the direct Chișinău–Tiraspol road crosses the de facto line and your CDW and third-party cover typically lapse the moment you do. If you intend to enter Transnistria by car you must buy the entity's own local insurance at the crossing; most travellers take a rutieră instead and leave the rental in Chișinău [VERIFY: current cross-border authorisation fee and Green Card charge at Chișinău desks].
raw.Road tax for foreign-plated cars: A **Moldovan-plated rental needs nothing** — road tax is already in the registration. A **foreign-plated car** must buy the ***vinieta***, an electronic road-use charge sold at the border crossings, at fuel stations and online at the state portal, in periods from seven days upward. It is checked by camera and by the border on exit; there is no sticker [VERIFY: current vinieta tariff bands].
raw.Viewpoints and laybys: The **Belvedere platform** above Butuceni over the Răut meander; the cliff terrace at **Țipova** above the Dniester with Ukraine on the far bank; the **Saharna** gorge above the 22 cascades; the **Soroca** riverfront below the fortress and the "Gypsy Hill" of mansions above the town; the R16 rise above **Cobani** for the Suta de Movile; the levee at **Slobozia Mare** over Lake Beleu at sunset.
